gloss: divide, share out, allot; portion, share; be smooth, flatter
summary: To divide and share out, and what falls to each: the land divided by lot among the tribes, spoil divided after victory, and חֵלֶק the portion, share or lot one has. Levi had no portion in the land because Yahweh was his portion (Num 18:20), Israel is Yahweh's portion (Deu 32:9), and the faithful say “Yahweh is my portion” (Psa 73:26; Lam 3:24); the dead have no more portion under the sun (Ecc 9:6). The same letters are also smooth: Jacob a smooth man beside hairy Esau, smooth stones from the wadi, and above all smooth speech, the flattering lips and tongue that deceive. Arabic ḫlq has both, a share or portion and smoothness, and Isaiah 57:6 sets the two side by side: “among the smooth stones of the wadi is your portion; they are your lot.”

words.gloss: divide, share out, apportion, allot; be smooth; (hiphil) make smooth, flatter
words.summary: About 65 times in six stems. Mostly “divide” in the sense of sharing out: land among tribes, spoil among victors, food among the people, men into courses. A few qal and hiphil uses are “be smooth, make smooth”, nearly always of speech. BDB files the same tokens under two verbs (h.da.aa “divide”, h.db.aa “be smooth”); this entry keeps one verb with both meanings, as the Arabic cognate does.

stems.gloss: divide, share; allot, assign; be smooth

senses.gloss: divide, share out, take a share
senses.definition: To divide something held in common so that each has his part: land, spoil, an inheritance, men into courses.

evidence.note: “As the חֵלֶק of the one who went down to battle, so the חֵלֶק of the one who stayed by the baggage: יַחֲלֹקוּ together.” Verb and noun side by side: to divide is to give each his חֵלֶק.
“As Yahweh commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did, וַיַּחְלְקוּ the land.”
“You and Ziba shall divide the field.”
“Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.”
An insightful servant “will share an inheritance among the brothers”.
“One who shares with a thief hates his life.”
Treasurers appointed “to distribute to their brothers”.
“They divided them by lots”: the priests into courses (מַחְלְקוֹת, v. 1).
David divided the Levites into divisions.
What the wicked piles up, “the innocent will divide the silver”.
Ahaz took a share from the house of Yahweh and the king's house to give to the king of Assyria.

senses.definition: Of God or a ruler: to give each his part, to assign.

evidence.note: Sun, moon and stars, “which Yahweh your God has allotted (חָלַק) to all the peoples under the whole heaven”.
“Gods they had not known, and he had not allotted to them.”
God “has not given her a share in understanding”, of the ostrich.
“You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and allotted them to every corner.”
The Levites “whom David had assigned over the house of Yahweh”.

senses.definition: Of speech or the heart: smooth, slippery, so that what is meant slides past.

evidence.note: “The butter of his mouth חָלְקוּ, but his heart was war; his words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.”
“Their heart חָלַק; now they shall bear their guilt”: slippery, false.

senses.definition: Of land shared out by lot, a people split in two, or light spread abroad.

evidence.note: “To these the land תֵּחָלֵק as an inheritance by the number of names.”
“Only by lot shall the land be divided.”
“The people of Israel were divided in half”, between Tibni and Omri.
“The way where the light is divided (spread)”.
Abram “divided himself against them by night”: split his force.

stems.gloss: divide, apportion; divide spoil; distribute; scatter

senses.definition: To divide land among those who will inherit it, by lot and line.

evidence.note: “Now divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes.”
“Joshua cast a lot for them in Shiloh before Yahweh, and there Joshua divided the land to the sons of Israel according to their divisions (מַחְלְקֹתָם).”
“So they finished dividing the land.”
“He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them by line; they shall possess it for ever.”
“You shall divide this land among you according to the tribes of Israel.”
“I will divide Shechem and measure out the valley of Succoth”; parallel מָדַד “measure”.
“To a rebel he divides our fields.”
The nations judged because they scattered Israel “and divided my land”.
“He will divide the land for a price.”

senses.definition: To share out plunder after victory: the victor's joy.

evidence.note: The enemy: “I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil.”
Benjamin “in the evening divides the plunder”.
“Are they not finding, dividing the spoil?”
“As they rejoice when they divide the spoil.”
“I will divide him a portion with the many, and with the strong he shall divide the spoil, because he poured out his soul to death.”
“She who stays at home divides the spoil.”
“Better a lowly spirit with the afflicted than to divide spoil with the proud.”
The stronger man overcomes him and “divides his spoils” (τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν): the picture of Isa 53:12.

senses.definition: Of those who crucified the Messiah: sharing out his clothing.

evidence.note: “They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots.”
John quotes Psa 22:19 as fulfilled by the soldiers: “they divided (διεμερίσαντο) my garments among them”.

senses.definition: To hand out to each a share.

evidence.note: David “distributed to all the people … to each a cake of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake”.
“How often does he distribute pains in his anger?”

senses.definition: To split a people up and spread them apart, as judgment.

evidence.note: Of Simeon and Levi: “I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them (וַאֲפִיצֵם) in Israel.”
“The face of Yahweh has divided them; he will no more regard them.”

senses.definition: Of spoil or land: to be shared out.

evidence.note: “Then the prey of a great spoil is divided; the lame take the plunder.”
“Your land shall be divided by line.”
“A day is coming for Yahweh, and your spoil shall be divided in your midst.”

senses.definition: Of the tribes sharing the land between them.

evidence.note: “They shall divide it among themselves into seven portions (חֲלָקִים).”

stems.gloss: make smooth, flatter; (once) take a share

senses.definition: To smooth metal with a hammer; and of the tongue or words, to make them smooth: to flatter and so deceive.

evidence.note: “The one who smooths (מַחֲלִיק) with the hammer, with him who strikes the anvil”: the literal act.
“There is no firmness in his mouth … their throat an open grave; they make their tongue smooth.”
Paul quotes Psa 5:10: “with their tongues they deceived (ἐδολιοῦσαν)”: smooth speech is deceit.
“The foreign woman who makes her words smooth.”
“He who rebukes a man will find more favour than one who makes his tongue smooth”: the opposite of rebuke.
“A man who flatters his neighbour spreads a net for his steps.”
“He flatters himself in his own eyes, too much to find out his iniquity and hate it.”

senses.definition: Once, of receiving a share of property.

evidence.note: Jeremiah went to the land of Benjamin “to take a share there (לַחֲלִק) among the people”, perhaps of family land (compare Jer 32:7–9).

evidence.locator: Psa.22.19, יְחַלְּקוּ → διεμερίσαντο; Ezk.47.21, חִלַּקְתֶּם → διαμερίσετε; διαμερίζω renders חָלַק ×10

evidence.note: “They divided (διεμερίσαντο) my garments among them”: Psa 22:19 quoted.

evidence.locator: Isa.53.12, יְחַלֵּק → μεριεῖ; Num.26.53, תֵּחָלֵק → μερισθήσεται; Jos.14.5 → ἐμέρισαν

evidence.note: “As the Lord has distributed (ἐμέρισεν) to each”: God allotting, as Deu 4:19.
“Tell my brother to divide (μερίσασθαι) the inheritance with me.”
Psa 5:10 quoted: “with their tongues they deceived”.

parallels.note: “Lot”: land is divided by lot, and the lot falls to each as his portion.
“Scatter”: dividing a people is scattering them.
“Measure out”: land divided is land measured.

opposites.note: “Rebuke”: plain correction against the smooth tongue.

words.gloss: portion, share; lot; tract of land; (once) smoothness
words.summary: About 66 times: what falls to someone when a whole is divided. A share of spoil or food, a tract of land, a share in a people or a king, and then one's lot in life. Its weightiest use is Yahweh as the portion of Levi and of the faithful, and Israel as Yahweh's portion. Once, Pro 7:21, it is “smoothness” of speech (BDB h.db.ab, the same tokens).

senses.definition: The part of spoil, food or offerings that is someone's due.

evidence.note: “As the portion of him who went down to battle, so the portion of him who stayed by the baggage.”
“The share of the men who went with me … let them take their share.”
“The half, the portion of those who went out to war.”
The grain offering: “I have given it as their portion from my offerings.”
The Levite “shall eat portion like portion” with his brothers.
“Give a portion to seven, or even to eight.”

senses.definition: A piece of land allotted to a tribe, a family or a man.

evidence.note: “To Caleb he gave a portion among the sons of Judah … Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron.”
They described the land “by cities in seven portions (חֲלָקִים)”, for the lot.
“The portion of the sons of Judah was too large for them.”
The holy contribution, “in length as one of the portions”, in the division of the land to come.
“Dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel.”
“He changes the portion of my people.”
The fire “devoured the great deep and was eating the portion”: the allotted land.

senses.gloss: share in (a people, a king, a city)
senses.definition: A part and a right in a family, a king's house, or a people: with negation, to have nothing to do with it.

evidence.note: “We have no portion in David, no inheritance in the son of Jesse; every man to his tents, Israel!”
Rachel and Leah: “Is there still any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?”
“You have no portion in Yahweh”: no part in his worship.
“You have no portion, no right, no memorial in Jerusalem.”
“Your portion is with adulterers”: you take part with them.
Peter to Simon: “You have no portion (μερίς) nor lot in this matter”, the words of Deu 12:12 and 14:27 of Levi.
“What portion (μερίς) has a believer with an unbeliever?”

senses.gloss: Yahweh as portion; Israel as Yahweh's portion
senses.definition: Levi received no portion of land because Yahweh himself was his portion; the faithful take up the words for themselves; and in turn Yahweh's own portion is his people.

evidence.note: To Aaron: “You shall have no portion among them; I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.”
“Levi has no portion nor inheritance with his brothers; Yahweh is his inheritance.”
“The Levites have no portion among you, for the priesthood of Yahweh is their inheritance.”
“Yahweh is the portion of my share and my cup; you hold my lot.”
“My flesh and my heart fail, but God is the rock of my heart and my portion for ever.”
“Yahweh is my portion; I have said I will keep your words.”
“You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.”
“Yahweh is my portion, says my soul; therefore I will hope in him.”
“For Yahweh's portion is his people; Jacob the lot of his inheritance.”
“Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for he is the former of all things.”
“Yahweh will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem.”
The Father “who has made us fit for a portion (μερίδα) of the lot of the saints in light”.

senses.definition: What a man receives in life, or what God deals out to him: reward or judgment.

evidence.note: “There is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion.”
“My heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.”
“That is your portion in life and in your toil.”
The dead: “they have no more portion for ever in anything done under the sun.”
“Men of the world, whose portion is in this life”, against v. 15, “I shall be satisfied when I awake with your likeness.”
“This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance appointed him by God”; parallel נַחֲלָה.
“This is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who rob us.”
“Instead of dishonour they shall rejoice in their portion; in their land they shall possess double.”
“Among the smooth stones (חַלְּקֵי) of the wadi is your portion (חֶלְקֵךְ); they, they are your lot (גּוֹרָלֵךְ)”: the idols she chose for her lot.
“By them his portion is fat.”
“I also will answer my part.”
“Mary has chosen the good portion (μερίδα), which shall not be taken from her.”

senses.definition: Smooth, persuasive words.

evidence.note: “With much persuasion she turns him; with the smoothness (בְּחֵלֶק) of her lips she drives him.”
“No portion nor lot” (οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος): the Septuagint's words for Levi, Deu 12:12; 14:27.
“A portion of the lot of the saints.”

parallels.note: “Inheritance”: “no portion nor inheritance”, the fixed pair for Levi, and the wicked man's portion and inheritance.
“Lot”: the portion is what the lot gives.
“Cup”: what is measured out to drink, beside the portion.

phrases.gloss: he has no portion or inheritance

words.summary: About 43 times, nearly all in Chronicles: the groups into which the tribes, or the priests, Levites, gatekeepers and the king's army, were divided, each serving in its turn.

senses.definition: The land as divided among the tribes.

evidence.note: “Joshua gave it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes.”
“This is the land you shall divide by lot to the tribes of Israel, and these are their divisions.”

senses.definition: One of the groups of priests, Levites or soldiers who served in rotation.

evidence.note: “David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi.”
“The divisions of the sons of Aaron.”
The king's army, “division by division coming in and going out month by month … each division 24,000”.
“The divisions of the gatekeepers.”
All the priests sanctified themselves “without keeping to the divisions”.
“Jehoiada did not dismiss the divisions.”

words.gloss: portion of ground, plot of field; smoothness, smooth words, slippery places
words.summary: About 24 times, in two senses that BDB files apart (h.da.ae, h.db.ad, the same tokens): a portion of ground, a plot of field, and smoothness, of a smooth neck, of flattering speech, and of slippery ground.

senses.definition: A piece of land belonging to someone, usually a field.

evidence.note: Jacob “bought the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent” for a hundred qesitah.
Joseph's bones buried “in the portion of the field that Jacob bought”.
“Her chance lighted on the portion of the field belonging to Boaz.”
“Naomi is selling the portion of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.”
“Joab's plot is next to mine, and he has barley there.”
“Throw him on the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.”
“Ruin every good plot with stones.”
“One plot was rained on, and the plot on which it did not rain withered.”
“They have trampled my portion; they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.”
Gad: “there the commander's portion was reserved.”

senses.definition: Smoothness of skin; and of the lips or tongue, flattery that deceives.

evidence.note: Kid skins put “on the smooth part of his neck”, so that Jacob would feel hairy like Esau (v. 11).
“They speak falsehood each to his neighbour, with lips of smoothness and a double heart they speak.”
“May Yahweh cut off all lips of smoothness.”
“From the smoothness of the tongue of a foreign woman.”
“Do not prophesy to us what is right; speak to us smooth things, prophesy illusions.”

senses.definition: Ground where the foot slips: where the wicked stand before they fall.

evidence.note: “Surely you set them in slippery places; you make them fall to ruin.”

senses.definition: Smooth to touch: skin without hair, stones worn by water, a bare mountain.

evidence.note: “Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.”
“Among the smooth (stones) of the wadi is your portion; they are your lot”: the smooth stones and the portion, one play on the root.
“From Mount Halak (הָהָר הֶחָלָק) that rises toward Seir”: the bare mountain.

senses.definition: Of mouth, palate or divination: smooth and pleasing, and so deceitful.

evidence.note: “The lips of a strange woman drip honey, and her palate is smoother than oil.”
“A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a smooth mouth works ruin.”
“There shall no more be any false vision or smooth (flattering) divination in the house of Israel.”

words.summary: The reduplicated form, “very slippery”: four times, of a way that makes the foot slide and of the smooth dealing by which the king of the north takes power.

senses.definition: A way so slippery that the walker falls.

evidence.note: “Their way shall be to them like slippery places in the darkness; they shall be driven on and fall in it.”
“Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of Yahweh pursuing them.”

senses.definition: Flattery and smooth promises used to win power or followers.

evidence.note: “A despised one … shall come in quietly and seize the kingdom by smooth dealings.”
“Many shall join themselves to them with smooth dealings.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, three times: the portion of the felled tree, Nebuchadnezzar, with the beasts, and the king's share in the province Beyond the River.

senses.definition: What falls to someone; a share in a land.

evidence.note: “Let his portion be with the beasts in the grass of the earth.”
“You will have no portion in the province Beyond the River.”

senses.definition: A section of the Levites by father's house, standing for each family of the people.

evidence.note: “Stand in the holy place by the divisions of the fathers' houses … and the division of a father's house of the Levites.”

senses.definition: Stones worn smooth by water.

evidence.note: David “chose five smooth stones from the wadi”.

senses.definition: Smooth words that lead into apostasy.

evidence.note: “Those who act wickedly against the covenant he will corrupt with flatteries, but the people who know their God shall be strong and act.”

words.gloss: Helkath, a Levitical city in Asher: “portion”
words.summary: A town on the border of Asher, given to the Gershonite Levites. The name is the noun חֶלְקָה “portion, plot of ground”. A place, so it has no name entry. BDB's tokens for it include every חֶלְקַת by spelling; only Jos 19:25 and 21:31 are the town.

senses.definition: A town on the border of Asher, a Levitical city.

evidence.note: “Their border was Helkath, Hali, Beten and Achshaph.”

words.gloss: Helkath-hazzurim, by the pool of Gibeon: “field of the blades”
words.summary: The place at Gibeon where twelve men of Benjamin and twelve of David's servants killed each other. The first word is חֶלְקָה “plot of ground”; the second is the plural of צוּר, here most simply “flints, blades” (compare צֹר “flint knife”, Exo 4:25), the swords each drove into his fellow's side. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: The field at Gibeon named for the combat of the twenty-four.

evidence.note: “Each caught his fellow by the head, with his sword in his fellow's side, and they fell down together; so that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.”

words.summary: The rock in the wilderness of Maon where Saul, closing round David, broke off to meet the Philistines. The name is the rock of הַמַּחְלְקוֹת: as the plural of מַחֲלֹקֶת, “the rock of divisions”, where the two parted; BDB reads it “smoothness”, the other sense of the root. The verse gives the event, not the meaning. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: A rock in the wilderness of Maon.

evidence.note: “Saul returned from pursuing David and went against the Philistines; therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth.”
Saul on one side of the mountain, David on the other: the two sides kept apart.

cognates.gloss: measure, determine the measure of (a hide, before cutting it); (ḫalāq) share, portion, a share of good
cognates.note: Lane gives measuring as the verb's primary meaning, of a leather-worker who measures a hide and then cuts it, and ḫalāq as “a share, or portion”: “there is no share for him in the final state” is the Hebrew's “no portion”. The later Arabic “create” grew from “measure out, proportion”. Arabic shows ḫ behind ח.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 799, art. خلق, خَلْقٌ (n11381)
evidence.note: “The act of measuring; or determining the measure, proportion, or the like, of a thing … this is the primary meaning”; خَلَقَ الأَدِيمَ, of a hide.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 802, art. خلق, خَلَاقٌ
evidence.note: “A share, or portion … لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُ فِى الآخِرَةِ There is no share, or portion, [of good] for him in the final state of existence.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 802, art. خلق, خَالِقٌ
evidence.note: “A worker in leather … because he measures first, and then cuts”; women working in leather “as engaged in dividing a hide”.
Inherited from Proto-Semitic *ḫalaq-, compared with Hebrew חָלַק “divide”, Syriac ܚܠܩ “divide, apportion” and Sabaean ḫlq “portion, lot”.

cognates.gloss: be smooth; smooth, smooth and solid (of stone, a rock, a mountain); smoothness; (of a garment) worn smooth
cognates.note: The same Arabic root, ḫ behind ח again: smooth stone and rock, smooth mountains, an arrow made smooth. This is the Hebrew's smooth skin, smooth stones of the wadi and bare Mount Halak, and with it the smooth tongue. Both Hebrew meanings show the same sound in the same Arabic root, so they belong together rather than to two older roots.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 802, art. خلق, أَخْلَقُ
evidence.note: “Smooth … smooth and solid … حَجَرٌ أَخْلَقُ Stone that is smooth … صَخْرَةٌ خَلْقَآءُ A rock … smooth.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 801, art. خلق, خَلَقٌ and خُلْقَةٌ
evidence.note: “The being smooth”; “Smoothness.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 802, art. خلق, خَوَالِقُ
evidence.note: “Smooth mountains”: compare הָהָר הֶחָלָק, Jos 11:17.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums: the noun is the Targum's word for the Hebrew חֵלֶק of Levi (Targ. Deu 14:27).

evidence.note: “Portion, share”, Targ. Deut. XIV, 27; Targ. Gen. XLVIII, 22; pl. Targ. Gen. XLVII, 24; Targ. Ez. XLVIII, 21.
“Lot, field”, Targ. Prov. XXIII, 10; Targ. Mic. II, 4 (for Hebrew שָׂדֵינוּ).

cognates.note: Classical Syriac; not in the Peshitta New Testament's vocabulary (SEDRA has no ܚܠܩ root), which uses ܡܢܬܐ for “portion”. Not yet checked in a Syriac dictionary.

evidence.note: “Lot, portion; fate, destiny; casting lots, oracles, auguries.”

cognates.note: Punic, in the name ʾšmnḥlq “Eshmun is my lot”, the same build as Hilkiah “my portion is Yahweh”.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ḥeleq] n.m. LOT, FATE (in personal names)”, Benz 71, ʾšmnḥlq, “Esmun is my lot”; “Cf. the Heb. personal name Ḥilqiyahu”.

evidence.locator: SEM000119 ḥlq [piece] N, PUN000681 ḥlq [lot] N

cognates.note: Ge'ez: counting as reckoning out shares. The link is argued in the Proto-Semitic list but the meaning is a step away. Ge'ez shows ḫ behind ח, as Arabic. Not yet checked in Dillmann or Leslau.

evidence.locator: SEM000118 ḥlq [part] V, GEZ002596 ḫwallaqwa [count] V

cognates.gloss: (Sabaean) part of an irrigation works, perhaps a water-distributor
cognates.note: Old South Arabian (Sabaean), once (C338/7); Biella compares Arabic ḫalaqa “measure” and Hebrew חָלַק and reads it as a “sharer-out” of water. Uncertain; shows ḫ behind ח.

evidence.note: “Part of irrigation apparatus (?) [Cf Ar ḫalaqa ‘measure’; Heb ḥālaq ‘divide, share.’ … ‘water-distributor’ or the like, a ‘measurer’ or ‘sharer-out’ of water.]”

doctrine.statement: Levi received no portion of the land, and Yahweh gave the reason: “I am your portion and your inheritance” (Num 18:20; Deu 10:9; 18:1–2). The psalmists take the same words for themselves: Yahweh is “the portion of my share and my cup”, “my portion for ever” when flesh and heart fail, “my portion in the land of the living” (Psa 16:5; 73:26; 142:6; Lam 3:24). And the relation runs both ways: “Yahweh's portion is his people” (Deu 32:9; Jer 10:16). The apostles carry the language on: Simon has “no portion nor lot” in the gospel, in the words said of Levi (Act 8:21), and the Father has made believers fit for “a portion of the lot of the saints” (Col 1:12). To have Yahweh as one's portion is to hold him as one's whole inheritance, above any share of the land now.

Ecclesiastes says what the dead have: “the dead know nothing, and they have no more reward … and they have no more portion for ever in anything that is done under the sun” (Ecc 9:5–6), and so “there is no work or device or knowledge or wisdom in the grave, where you are going” (9:10). A man's portion is in his life and his toil (Ecc 3:22; 9:9). Nothing in these verses gives the dead a portion elsewhere; their portion ends at death. The hope is not in a portion after death but in waking: the men of the world have “their portion in this life”, but the psalmist says, “I shall behold your face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied when I awake with your likeness” (Psa 17:14–15), awaking from the sleep of death at the resurrection (Dan 12:2).

The land was divided to the tribes by lot before Yahweh (Num 26:53–56; Jos 18:10), and the division is promised again: Ezekiel's vision divides the land “according to the tribes of Israel”, with the sojourners inheriting among them and the prince's portion beside the holy contribution (Ezk 47:21–22; 48:8, 29; 45:7). Yahweh “will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem” (Zec 2:16), and he will gather the nations and judge them because they scattered Israel “and divided my land” (Jol 4:2). What Yahweh once divided by lot he will divide again: the land is a literal inheritance still to be given in the kingdom of God.

Two of the root's verses are fulfilled in Jesus. “They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots” (Psa 22:19) was done by the soldiers at the cross, “that the scripture might be fulfilled” (Jhn 19:24). And the servant of Isaiah 53 is given his portion only after his death: “I will divide him a portion with the many, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong, because he poured out his soul to death” (Isa 53:12). The servant's soul is poured out to death, so he truly died; his share of the spoil comes after, when God raised him and exalted him (Php 2:8–9), and Jesus himself spoke of the stronger man who overcomes and “divides his spoils” (Luk 11:22).

note: One spelling, one entry: BDB files חלק as two roots (h.da.* “divide”, h.db.* “be smooth”) and lists the verb and חֵלֶק and חֶלְקָה twice over the same tokens; each is one word here with senses for both, named by the h.da key only. The cognates show ḫ behind ח for both meanings (Arabic ḫlq “share, measure” and “smooth”; Ge'ez and Sabaean ḫ for the dividing sense), so the split in the dictionaries is not supported by the sounds; Isa 57:6 puns on the two (smooth stones / portion / lot), and Jastrow's lead that חֵלֶק was first the smooth stone cast as a lot (1Sa 17:40; Isa 34:17) is not proved by any verse; open question. Not recorded: Akkadian ḫalāqu and Ugaritic ḫlq “perish, be lost” (Oracc; Segert p. 186), linked by Wiktionary, which share neither meaning; Lam 4:16 (piel, “the face of Yahweh has divided them”) is the only use that leans that way, and its parallel Gen 49:7 “divide … scatter” explains it. Arabic ḥlq “shave; ring; throat” (Lane p. 628) is the other ḥ and not this root. Syriac ḥelqā and Ge'ez ḫwallaqwa still to check in Payne Smith / Brockelmann and Dillmann / Leslau. Names: Hilkiah, Helek (with the gentilic חֶלְקִי) and Helkai have name entries; the places Helkath, Helkath-hazzurim and Sela-hammahlekoth are words here. BDB h.db.ah (Sela-hammahlekoth, 4 tokens) and h.da.ah (Helkath, 12) are filed by spelling, so most of their tokens are the nouns מַחֲלֹקֶת and חֶלְקָה; m.bn.as is a zero-token cross-reference left unassigned. Hebrew צוּר in Helkath-hazzurim belongs to its own root's entry.
